Replay

Speedball party menus

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Saved party recovery

Set RSB_ROOM_SERVICE to use the shared Replay Party helper and room service. The native/browser menu then offers Create Party, Join Party, a Watch only choice, Rejoin Recent and Copy Invite. The creator can also copy its invite during play. Without that setting, the existing direct address and native save/resume menus remain available. Solo remains available in party mode; file selection/resume controls use the direct menu configuration.

The service URL is deployment configuration, not a hard-coded public service. A local development setup can use:

Shell
mkdir -p .replay-room-data
REPLAY_ROOM_CONTENT=0x5253504545444234 \
REPLAY_ROOM_DB="$PWD/.replay-room-data/speedball.sqlite3" \
REPLAY_ROOM_CREATE_DB=1 REPLAY_ROOM_LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT=1 \
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_room_service/run.sh

RSB_ROOM_SERVICE=ws://127.0.0.1:49740 RSB_ROOM_LOCAL=1 \
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/play.sh

Omit database creation on subsequent service starts. Give each local player a separate RSB_PROFILE, RSB_ROOMS_DB and RSB_PORT. Native storage currently uses the optional Darwin/Linux SQLite adapter. The game test uses verified WSS with a private CA; plain WS requires the explicit loopback development setting.

Setting Meaning
RSB_ROOM_SERVICE Provisioning and Room control URL
RSB_ROOM_LOCAL=1 Explicit loopback WS development mode
RSB_ROOM_CA Optional native CA certificate for private verified WSS
RSB_ROOMS_DB Room credentials and recent selection; default user://speedball_rooms.sqlite3
RSB_ROOM_ADDRESS Advertised native gameplay address; default 127.0.0.1
RSB_PORT This member's advertised gameplay port; default 49480
RSB_PROFILE Separate personal identity/name profile

The service needs reachable gameplay endpoints for native ENet. Local tests do not prove Internet/NAT traversal. The shared helper also accepts ICE/relay configuration, and the browser test verifies local RTC gameplay. Public deployment and TURN-only routing remain separate Speedball acceptance work.

Create Party durably enrolls a creator and produces a repeatable invite. Join Party validates the pasted invite, enrolls the member and durably stores its credential before opening Room. Rejoin Recent reads that stored credential; the returned process receives a newer incarnation and retains its game seat. The personal identity/name profile remains separate from the room's network token. A failed invitation does not create a local game; competing start actions are blocked while enrollment is active.

Invites grant trusted co-op membership with SEATS - 1 uses. The menu explicitly says invited friends can host and keep the match running. This grants access to complete authority checkpoints when selected as a successor. It is not a competitive untrusted-player preset. Ordinary player invitations remain a library capability; this game menu currently issues the trusted co-op variant.

Watch only applies to Join Party and Rejoin Recent. Invited observers occupy seat 0, create no player, and receive no checkpoints. They remain observers through migration and can leave/rejoin in that mode. Observer chat uses the existing Observer label. The choice is a gameplay role, not a reduction of the credential's underlying trusted membership; the driver selects successors from connected player seats. Create Party starts a player host regardless of the watch choice.

Room's normal lease/roster checks, automatic successor selection, prepared checkpoints and migration UI apply. Native acceptance saves a moving scored pitch, performs planned handoff or abrupt owner loss, then returns the old host in a fresh process using Rejoin Recent. It requires a stable invite/seat, an increased incarnation, observer leave/rejoin, new spikes/chat and matching canonical worlds.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/online_run.sh
RSB_PARTY_RENDER=1 RSB_PARTY_MODES=planned \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/online_run.sh

RSB_PARTY_OUT selects a fresh artifact directory. Private databases, identity files, TLS keys and invite text belong in local scratch storage, not published test results. See receipts, captures and limits.

Steam integration, invite rotation/revocation UI, public deployment and wider visual/playtest/comparison coverage remain. The original Speedball and sibling Scrapyard projects stay independently runnable.

The browser party gate exports the same game and uses lower-case query parameters such as room_service / room_local instead of native environment variables. It persists personal identity/name and room credentials in separate IndexedDB namespaces, and verifies them after closing/reopening a browser process. Gameplay uses WebRTC while the configured service provides enrollment, control and signaling. The local gate exercises planned handoff, browser-host loss, true observers, rejoin, new actions/chat and matching worlds. See browser evidence for measured limits. Browser solo checkpoints use the separate save-slot flow; public relay deployment remains open.

Saved party recovery#

The online host can use Save or F5 to publish the match to the room service. Saving is asynchronous: the UI shows progress, a confirmed stored tick, or an uncertain result that can be retried. Followers and observers cannot publish. RSB_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MS (browser room_checkpoint_ms) opts into automatic saving; zero keeps saves manual and supported intervals are 1–120 seconds.

Rejoin recent party joins a live host when one exists. If the party is abandoned, Room loads the stored match, obtains a newer authority epoch and resumes it with the returning player's stable seat/profile. Missing, incompatible or too-old saves show a recovery error and retry option. A stored save does not bypass the room's rollback policy or create a replacement match silently.

The recovery fixture saves a scored first round, exits the game and kills/restarts the service, then uses the actual rejoin menu in a fresh process. It checks the saved score, winner, round and kick count plus personal profile identity, admits a new guest, plays round 2, verifies chat and publishes again. A separate reader validates the continued stored match and names.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/party_restore_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_speedball/party_restore_web_run.sh

Native uses verified TLS; the browser fixture uses explicit loopback development WS and real RTC. These checkpoints remain distinct from direct file saves and browser solo slots. See Room restoration.

The recovery notice uses the shared backup-status observation. It distinguishes an approved backup from preparation, stale progress or uncertain control; a prior host change does not imply the next backup is ready.
